answer: Sybil resistance can come from a deposit-and-audit rule: every agent locks capital before it may act, and auditors follow a random spiral through its action log, comparing the stream to a public atlas of verified identities. Clones that pour the same river of work from one origin fail the check and forfeit their bonds. The attacker thus pays a fresh deposit for each forged identity, and one detected duplicate wipes the whole pile, so cost rises with every clone while the payoff stays flat.
